name: OA.Works
tagline: Powerfully simple open access tools for a just and kind information age
dependency_risks: fiscal sponsorship dependency on Code for Science & Society
reliance on publisher permissions data accuracy

policy_outcomes.description: Plan S Journal Checker Tool launched using OA.Works permissions data
OA.Report adopted by cOAlition S member organisations for open access compliance tracking
RSCVD built in partnership with IFLA as free international interlibrary loan system during COVID; IFLA took over long-term running in 2024

outcome_methodology: Usage metrics (millions of tool uses documented); compliance tracking for cOAlition S; partnership-based co-design with librarians
documented_limitations: Sunsetting of Open Access Button and InstantILL announced (2025)
curation_criteria: Tools built in partnership with librarians and open access advocates; values-driven product decisions
contributor_governance: Open source repositories; Advisory Committee oversees strategy
disparity_tracking: Implicit through focus on research equity and global access; tools designed to reduce barriers for researchers in lower-income countries and under-resourced institutions
community_ownership: Community-governed via Advisory Committee; open source code

government_partnerships.description: Co-developed RSCVD international interlibrary loan system; IFLA assumed long-term operation in 2024

political_relevance_summary: OA.Works addresses barriers to research access and knowledge equity, promoting open access to publicly funded research that informs policy and civic understanding.

movement_building_utility.notes: OA.Works primarily serves as an information resource for researchers, journalists, or analysts working on civic and political issues.

generalizability_notes: High generalizability. OA.Works is open source and already deployed across multiple countries/jurisdictions, making replication straightforward for other contexts.
